title: Records Galore as Sanlam Cape Town Marathon Becomes Africa's Fastest
claims: Three of the four course records were broken at the 2026 Sanlam Cape Town Marathon.
Mohamed Esa won the men's race in 2:04:55, breaking the previous course record of 2:08:16 set by Abdisa Tola in 2024.
The first 10 men all finished under the previous course record; Esa's time is described as the fastest marathon ever run on African soil and a new South African All-comers record.
Dera Dida won the women's race in 2:23:18, just under a minute outside Glenrose Xaba's course record of 2:22:22 from 2024.
Mestawut Fikir was second in 2:23:46 and Waganesh Amare third in 2:23:57.
David Weir won the men's wheelchair race in 1:30:20, inside Gert Schipper's previous course record of 1:32:09 from 2023.
Manuela Schär won the women's wheelchair race in 1:43:25, breaking Eden Rainbow-Cooper's previous course record of 1:52:58 from 2023.
Dida said wind and curves in the route made the women's course record difficult to attack.
Weir said early-morning humidity affected his breathing for the first couple of miles.
The article describes the 2026 field as the fastest ever assembled for an African marathon and notes that Major status requires a field including World Athletics Platinum and Gold Label athletes.
